why: Intro to Git plan, 'Undo a change and ignore files' (keep .DS_Store out of the cookbook for good). The learner wrote .gitignore correctly but staged with `git add .` instead of `git add .gitignore`, so the commit 'Ignore .DS_Store' shows 'create mode 100644 .DS_Store': the file the step keeps out is now tracked, and .gitignore never untracks a file that is already committed. The .gitignore line and the commit row are both there; the step's point is not.

step.title: Ignore .DS_Store for good
step.instructions: Make a .gitignore that lists .DS_Store: echo .DS_Store > .gitignore. Stage only that file with git add .gitignore and commit it with git commit -m "Ignore .DS_Store". .DS_Store itself must never be committed.
